question: Can a concentration-guided one-pair query select a useful local certificate without examining all overlaps or the full allowed set?
status: Known-control diagnostic; general arguments remain HYPOTHESIS/proof candidates; no novelty claim
input_contract: A prescribed three-speed core plus four distinct positive residual speeds; core selection itself is not solved. All frozen full speed lists have gcd1 and retain the original unit period.
selection_rule: Construct the complete closed safe set of only the supplied core on [0,1], retaining singleton components and counting construction cost.
Among positive-length core components select the widest, breaking ties by smallest left endpoint. Never change this window after seeing residual data.
Compute the four individual blocking durations D on the selected window using endpoint primitives; E=sum(D)-window_length.
Rank the six pairs by descending min(D_i,D_j), then ascending numerical speed pair. This is an overlap upper cap, not a prediction or lower bound.
If E<0, certify positive duration from singles and make no overlap query. Otherwise if the largest cap is at most E, record that no one-pair bound can be positive and make no overlap query.
Otherwise query exactly the first ranked pair's overlap O and use lower bound O-E. Never rerank or query another pair after failure.

If no positive duration certificate resulted, test only the selected window's right endpoint against all seven nonreference speeds. If valid, record its shared safe-lap intersection and equality directions to distinguish a positive local interval from an isolated contact. If invalid, return uncertified and stop the ordered diagnostic campaign. Do not select a second endpoint or window.
overlap_evaluator: After selecting a<b, choose h in {1,2} minimizing (abs(b-h*a),h); put r=b-h*a. Use signed-residual phase strips and the exact periodic endpoint primitive. Count all strips and primitive calls. This is an evaluation choice, not a pair-ranking score. The independent verifier uses direct blocking-interval intersection instead.
validation_contract: Exact rational arithmetic only; no time/phase grid or broad speed search.
Primary generator must not read full allowed sets, all-pair archives, benchmark durations, or the independent implementation.

Independent verifier may read schema/output/protocol but must not read/import primary implementation. Use a separately structured core event partition, direct chosen-pair interval intersections, and endpoint substitution.
Compare policy outputs afterward to already archived local actual durations and best-pair/tree bounds. Benchmark sources do not feed selection. No new full seven-runner safe-set reconstruction.
These are known controls informed by prior research, not blind or held-out validation. Preserve the first uncertified result without retuning.
cost_contract: Count core laps/events/components, four single-duration primitive calls at two endpoints each, six scalar pair caps, at most one exact overlap evaluation with all residual-strip construction and primitive calls, and at most one seven-runner endpoint plus its safe-lap intersection. Report rational operand bit sizes separately. No uniform or empirical runtime speedup claim follows merely from the one-query count.
scope_limits: No arbitrary-speed existence guarantee, no core-selection theorem, no complete strictness classification, no external proof certification or novelty assertion. A failed policy is not failed loneliness. +7/+9 and cutoff polishing remain parked.
